kind.description: WHICH class of evidence this finding rests on. `deprecation` is a surface the contract says is GOING AWAY — an operation, parameter or body field a call used, or one a replacement document newly deprecated. It is its own kind rather than a warning-severity live-vs-spec or version-diff because nothing has failed: the call conformed, so a deprecation never marks its call drifted and never counts as live drift.

change_kind.description: WHAT moved — a FINER axis than `kind`, which names which detector spoke. Additive and OPTIONAL: set on MCP findings only (definition_change carries wording|input|output|catalog, output_mismatch carries value, stale_client carries observed_failure); absent on the HTTP/OpenAPI kinds and on findings from older collectors, so readers must tolerate its absence. A kind never implies a severity.

via_dispatch.description: Additive and optional: the dispatcher tool a call went through when detection attributed it to the inner tool a recorded search result named.

source.description: Additive and optional: which contract the finding was judged against — tools_list (a complete observed catalog; absence means this), search_result (definitions a discovery meta-tool returned) or toolset_enable (a session's listing right after a toolset was enabled).

completeness.description: Additive and optional: complete, or partial — a search result is partial by nature and never a source of removals.
